exclude.basis: Milky Way foreground stars, by the criterion of Ren et al. (2021, Sect. 3.2): a Gaia parallax measured to better than 20% that places the star within 50 kpc (parallax above 0.02 mas), or a proper motion in right ascension or declination above 0.2 mas/yr (500 km/s at M33) plus 2 sigma, measured to better than 20%. Applied to Gaia DR3 (they used DR2) within 0.75 deg of M33's centre, which covers the LGGS field (0.72 deg); an LGGS star within 1 arcsec of one is left out, the radius Ren et al. match LGGS to UKIRT with. Reading their equations (1) and (2) as either component.

frame.converter: Each sky position onto the midplane of the inclined disc M33's image layers are baked on (recipe.json), through the image-layer bake's own intersection.

discThickness.basis: Ciardullo et al. (2004, Sect. 6) adopt z0 ≈ 175 pc (at least ±25%) for the isothermal sheet sech²(z/z0) of M33's planetary nebulae, and their data exclude z0 ≲ 90 pc beyond 6 kpc. It is the only M33 disc scale height these sources state; young tracers (HII regions, Cepheids, clusters) are thinner in disc galaxies, so for them it is an upper value, used as a presentation choice. Each row's own height is drawn, not measured.

meaning: Stars of M33 in the Local Group Galaxies Survey (Massey et al. 2006), UBVRI photometry over the whole optical disc, after the Gaia foreground cut: one dot per star at its catalogue sky position, coloured by its measured B-V. The survey is limited by crowding in the bright centre, so its density there is a floor.

colorByBv.basis: Measured B-V, observed (not dereddened), through the app's catalogue star colour so these dots match its stars. The range covers M33's blue and red supergiants; a colour beyond it takes the end colour.

appearance.note: Presentation only: the Milky Way hot-star layer's size and opacity.
